language.script_notes: English signage throughout, with some Irish and Ulster Scots signs in places — far less systematic than Welsh bilingual signage in Wales.
false_friends: Ireland (shares the island and much of the landscape)

road_furniture.curb_style: In some estates kerbstones are painted in red, white and blue or green, white and orange to mark territory.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: UK-style mph speed limits, circular utility-pole attachments and 'GIVE WAY' text distinguish it from the Republic of Ireland, which uses km/h, rectangular attachments and 'YIELD'.

architecture.roof_style: Steeply pitched slate roofs with chimney stacks on terraces; simple pitched farmhouse roofs in the countryside.
architecture.roof_material: Slate and clay tile; corrugated metal on farm buildings.
architecture.wall_construction: Red-brick terraced houses are extremely common, especially in Belfast; whitewashed farmhouses and stone walls in the countryside; political murals painted on the gable ends of terraces in working-class areas of Belfast and Derry.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Red brick, grey stone, and whitewashed walls.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Red-brick terraces with gable-end murals (loyalist and republican); flags flying from lamp posts; peace walls in Belfast; whitewashed rural farmhouses.

nature.vegetation: Lush green pasture divided by hedgerows and stone walls; peat bog and heather on the uplands.
nature.terrain: Rolling drumlin farmland, the Mourne Mountains, the Antrim coast and the shores of Lough Neagh and Strangford Lough.
nature.climate_signature: Mild, damp maritime — green and often overcast.

vehicles.plate_color: UK plates — white front, yellow rear — though Northern Ireland plates often carry distinctive letter formats.
vehicles.plate_format: Northern Ireland uses its own registration format, generally with 'I' or 'Z' in the letters, unlike the standard GB format.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: The standard UK mix with a strong presence of farm vehicles in the countryside.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Dense coverage of towns and roads, including Belfast and rural lanes.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shares the island, with nearly identical green farmland, hedgerows and houses
confusion_set.tiebreaker: UK circular pole attachments versus Ireland's rectangular ones; blue versus green distance markers; mph versus km/h speed signs; 'GIVE WAY' versus 'YIELD'; UK yellow rear plates and gable-end political murals.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national road furniture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Northern Ireland has occasional Irish and Ulster Scots signs, painted kerbs and gable-end murals, and lacks Welsh bilingual signs or Scottish Gaelic road signs.
